dedupe_keys.name: region stockholm simulation based table top exercises to develop and test hospital evacuation plans

description: This case study reports how two emergency hospitals in Region Stockholm, Sweden, used a validated simulation system for table-top exercises to develop, test and revise their hospital evacuation plans. The authors published the work as an open-access journal article. Hospital medical staff, prehospital staff and partner agencies played their usual roles in real time, while moveable magnetic symbols on whiteboards represented actual patients, staff and transport resources; observers and instructors documented decisions and post-exercise surveys collected participants' views. Coverage is two hospitals and their surrounding response system in one Swedish region. The article is freely available under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the simulation is a manual exercise system, not computer software, results are qualitative, and only two hospitals took part. The study found that the method let planners test the whole evacuation process and identified improvement areas in management and liaison, communication, logistics, medical care and patient prioritisation, and resource use. Simulation uses: a reference for designing emergency response and evacuation exercises for hospitals and for checking computer simulation models of hospital evacuation against practitioner experience. Related records: the Hurricane Sandy hospital evacuations study (case_study-hurricane-sandy-nyc-hospital-evacuations) documents a real evacuation, and the North Shore-LIJ Hurricane Irene evacuation (case_study-hurricane-irene-nslij-hospital-evacuation) another.
